_: CANONICAL TUNING. Every implementation reads or is checked against this file.
_why: The same rules exist in sim/*.py, proto/index.html and unity/Assets/Scripts/Core/*.cs. Without one source of truth they drift, and this project's main asset is that its numbers are trustworthy. Run sim/check_drift.py to verify agreement.

loudness_constants._note: A dash in the spec's dDisturbance column is a hard zero. Walking is free.

disturbance._source: DESIGN.md 6.5, tuned LOOP_LOG R4, crew-scaled R12
disturbance._lever_cooldown_note: RETIRED in R19, kept only so sim/disturbance.py reproduces R18's figures. Do not implement. A carried charge is self-limiting by count, which is what the cooldown was faking.
disturbance._lever_note: R19. Levers are CONSUMABLES bought between nights and carried as cargo -- they cost van slots up front and nothing at the moment you pull one. Priced in throughput instead (R18's assumption), they are dominated: a crew that does the arithmetic never pulls one, because throughput and cargo are the same currency and retrieval only takes a fraction of what you carry, so paying loot to protect loot can never be favourable. In slots there is an interior optimum: 1 charge is +2.6%, 2 is break-even, 6 is -22%, and COLLECT time falls from 26% of the night to 8%.
disturbance._crew_note: R18. Was 1.0 (strictly linear, R12). Swept: linear leaves a solo crew hunted far harder than a full one -- 28% of the night at COLLECT against 17% -- because the sources that do NOT scale with headcount (the ratcheting floor, the dolly, the radio) are a much larger share of one player's noise budget. At 0.8 the profile is flat: 18/16/15/17% across 1/2/3/4 players. Two effects, not one: sources must scale per-player AND decay must scale sub-linearly.

attention._note: MULTIPLICATIVE. Additive constants let an empty-handed player be hunted 100% of the time.

van._ceiling_note: The appraiser's edge hits zero between 24 and 32 slots. The ceiling is a guarantee, not a knob.
van._ruin_note: Tail risk, not a fee. A linear cost cannot balance a multiplicative benefit.

appraiser._why: The appraiser's payoff is E[max of 4] - E[random] = 0.6 x spread x room mean. It is a property of the ROOM, not a global constant. A flat estate prices it at one number everywhere, which is why it read as a thin +6% edge for eight rounds.
appraiser._share_note: Per wing, not per estate. Below ~10% curio the mechanic stops paying (+6.2%); the validator's V11 enforces 15-35%.
appraiser._telegraph: Room class must be readable from the doorway without scanning. Unreadable dressing turns a decision into a coin flip.

concealment._why: 8.1 specified concealment in prose only. These are the values that make all four responses to being hunted -- run, hide, stash, hand off -- each correct somewhere. Modelled in sim/hiding.py.
concealment._search_note: 8-24s, and the WIDTH is the mechanic. A fixed give-up time is learnable, and a learnable one turns stashing into a formality: at a fixed 12-18s the stash timer always outlasts the search and saves the item 100% of the time, which is D-03's free-aggro-reset exploit re-entered through a different door. At 8-24s it saves 75%.
concealment._span_note: A stash within this distance of the item's home plinth is on the Curator's route (A4) and gets found. Stash safety is positional, not temporal.

progression._quota_note: R21. The previous curve (7500/9000/10750/12500) was calibrated on a model that ENDED THE NIGHT WHEN THE VAN FILLED; real crews swap up instead of leaving, which is worth ~42%, and every night passed 100% under it. R20 recalibrated but did so BEFORE re-banding the apex, so its curve (13250/15250/17250/19000) was stale against the final configuration by the time the round ended -- caught by chain_sim.py now printing measured pass rates against their calibration targets. This curve reproduces 96/73/59/38%.
progression._apex_note: R20, third setting of this band. At 4000-8000 the apex is a TRAP again: five indivisible slots plus a large labour block, measured at -3.8% against not taking it, because those five slots would otherwise be upgraded all night. Five marginal slots are worth ~$3,418 by sunrise (~$684/slot) and the labour costs the rest. At 6000-11000 it is +9.1% -- worth taking, cheap enough to skip on a bad night.
